intro: Hair fall has many causes and they need different treatments. Pattern hair loss driven by genetics and hormones, sudden shedding after illness, fever, childbirth or stress, iron and vitamin D deficiency, thyroid problems, PCOS, dandruff and scalp inflammation, patchy autoimmune loss and damage from tight hairstyles all present as 'hair fall', and treating the wrong one wastes months.

Hair and scalp problems are a special interest of Dr. Daksha Patel, an MD dermatologist with 17+ years of experience. Every hair consultation at Skin Essence includes trichoscopy, a magnified examination of the scalp and hair roots that distinguishes thinning from shedding, and blood tests where the history suggests a deficiency or hormonal cause.

Treatment is then built around the diagnosis: topical or low-dose oral minoxidil, finasteride or other anti-androgens where appropriate, correction of deficiencies, treatment of dandruff and scalp inflammation, and PRP for extra support. Pune's hard water, pollution and long working hours are factored into a routine you can actually follow. Results take time, so we review with photographs every three months.
whoIsItFor: Sudden, heavy shedding after illness, fever, surgery, childbirth or a stressful period
A receding hairline or thinning crown in men, or a widening parting in women
Hair fall with dandruff, itching or an oily, inflamed scalp
Patchy hair loss, which needs early treatment
Teenagers and young adults with early thinning, and anyone told to 'just use oil'

howItWorks.title: Consultation and trichoscopy
howItWorks.description: We take a detailed history of the shedding, your diet, medicines, stress and family pattern, and examine the scalp and roots under magnification.

howItWorks.title: Tests where needed
howItWorks.description: Blood tests for iron stores, vitamin D, vitamin B12, thyroid and, in women, hormonal markers identify correctable causes.

howItWorks.title: Treatment plan
howItWorks.description: Topical or oral medicines, supplements only where deficient, a scalp routine for dandruff, and lifestyle changes are set out in a written plan.

howItWorks.title: Review and escalation
howItWorks.description: Progress is reviewed with photographs at three months. PRP is added for extra density where useful, and transplant is discussed only for established pattern baldness.

sessionsAndDowntime.results: Shedding reduces in 6–12 weeks; regrowth visible in 4–6 months

aftercare: Use medicines every day as prescribed; hair treatment works slowly and stops working when stopped.
Wash the scalp two to three times a week with the shampoo advised; a clean scalp grows better hair than an oiled one.
Eat enough protein and correct deficiencies with the supplements prescribed, not a random handful of pills.
Avoid tight hairstyles, heat styling and chemical treatments while the hair recovers.

faqs.a: Shedding from stress, illness or deficiency usually stops once the trigger is corrected, and hair regrows over months. Pattern hair loss can be slowed and partly reversed with medicines and PRP, but needs ongoing treatment to hold the result.

Topical minoxidil can cause temporary extra shedding in the first weeks and scalp irritation. Low-dose oral minoxidil is an option for some patients and its effects are discussed before starting. Both must be used consistently.

Finasteride is effective for male pattern hair loss and well tolerated by most men. Side effects are uncommon and reversible on stopping, and are explained at consultation. It is not prescribed to women who may become pregnant.

faqs.q: Will hair oils, onion juice or special shampoos help?
faqs.a: Oils condition the hair shaft but do not treat the cause of hair fall, and heavy oiling can worsen dandruff. Shampoos help scalp conditions. Regrowth needs treatment of the actual cause.

faqs.q: How long before I see results?
faqs.a: Shedding usually reduces within 6 to 12 weeks. New growth is visible at 4 to 6 months, which is why we review with photographs rather than day-to-day impressions.
